public_rationale: Microsoft explicitly reports additions totaling approximately 2 GW over the two quarters identified in the post. That is substantial counterevidence. But Zitron disputes whether those additions were operational, and the cited statements do not define the measure sufficiently to settle that distinction. His inability to identify enough facilities also does not establish that Microsoft added less.
limitations: Accepting reported capacity as operational capacity would change the assessment.

statement.excerpt: How much actual capacity has Microsoft brought online? Because it certainly isn’t fucking 2GW in six months.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

our_interpretation: The full post explicitly links the roughly 2 GW comparison to Microsoft's FY2026 second- and third-quarter earnings statements. Use October 2025–March 2026, rather than a rolling six-month window or November–April.
Read 'actual capacity ... brought online' as equipped operational data-center capacity available for workloads, including owned and leased facilities.
Treat 2 GW as approximate because the referenced first-quarter contribution was described as nearly one gigawatt.
Do not equate a reported capacity addition with operational capacity unless its definition establishes that connection.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish that Microsoft added materially less than approximately 2 GW of equipped operational capacity during October 2025–March 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish that Microsoft added approximately 2 GW or more of equipped operational capacity during October 2025–March 2026.
